subject: Long-context evaluation next steps / model fit for Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Thompson <sam.thompson@acmehealth.com>, James Park <james.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Long-context evaluation next steps / model fit for Acme Health

Hi Sam / James,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand your clinical summarization workflow and the 200–500k token patient records you need summarized per week. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Recap (from our discovery)
- Primary goal: high-fidelity summarization of long clinical notes (up to ~512k tokens) with strict preservation of critical findings and no hallucinations.
- Key constraints: PHI handling, truncation behavior at > context length, throughput target ~50 summaries/hour, and cost sensitivity.

Model fit & recommendation (initial)
- Shortlist: redwood-llamax-65b (24k context variant) for latency/cost balance; redwood-extend-64b (128k context) for fidelity on longest records.
- For archival/very long runs, we recommend chunk+KV-cache + summarization-merge pipeline (we can provide prompt sets).

Evaluation artifacts I attached:
- prompt_set_v1.txt — initial prompt & chaining prompts we propose for your summarization spec.
- redwood_benchmark_summary.pdf — our internal benchmarks focusing on long-context latency/fidelity tradeoffs.

Questions / asks for you
1) Can you share a small (synthetic or redacted) sample of 3 long records (approx 50–200k tokens each) for a short pilot?
2) Are we ok to run a 48–72 hour pilot on Hosted with evaluation telemetry enabled?

Proposed next steps
- If you share samples, Laura (cc'd) will run the initial quality pass and return a brief CSV with ROUGE/QA checks and examples.
- We’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up next Thu to review results and tune prompts.

Attached: prompt_set_v1.txt, redwood_benchmark_summary.pdf

Thanks — I’m happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few follow-ups before we send samples: 

1) Truncation behavior: if a record exceeds the model context length, what does Redwood do by default? Does it drop the head, the tail, or is there automatic chunking + KV caching? We need determinism for QA.
2) Summarization fidelity: you mentioned QA checks — can you share the exact metrics you’ll run (ROUGE variants, factual QA checks)? Will you return flagged hallucinations?
3) Pilot scope: 48–72 hours sounds good — can we limit it to hosted with telemetry and make sure data is scoped to our account only? Also, any cost estimate for the pilot?

If you can send a short plan answering the three points I’ll get legal ready for sample sharing.

—Sam
Sam Thompson
Head of Clinical Data Platforms | Acme Health
sam.thompson@acmehealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Thompson <sam.thompson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: James Park <james.park@acmehealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Long-context evaluation next steps / model fit for Acme Health

Thanks Sam — answers inline and plan below. Laura — looping you in to run the pilot once Sam confirms.

1) Truncation behavior (default & options)
- Default: Redwood will not silently drop critical sections. For hosted endpoints we default to a configurable chunking strategy: chunk by semantic boundaries (paragraphs/sections) + KV caching across chunks when supported by the model.
- Options: drop-head, drop-tail, sliding-window, and chunk+merge. For your use case we recommend chunk+kv-cache + summarization-merge to preserve start/end clinical findings.

2) Summarization fidelity & evaluation metrics
- We run: ROUGE-1/2/L, BERTScore, and a targeted QA suite (question-answer pairs derived from gold annotations) to detect factual regressions.
- We also compute hallucination flags via contradiction detection and return example span-level mismatches. Output: CSV with per-case scores + flagged sentences.

3) Pilot scope & cost
- Hosted-only pilot, telemetry enabled, data scoped to your org (no cross-customer caching).
- Estimated cost: ~ $350–700 depending on model variant and number of tokens processed (we’ll give a firm quote once you share sample sizes).

Proposed pilot plan (if you approve)
- Day 0: Acme shares 3 redacted samples.
- Day 1–2: Laura runs model runs (redwood-llamax-65b and redwood-extend-64b), collects ROUGE/BERTScore/QA, and prepares long_context_eval_results.csv.
- Day 3: 30-min review to decide production path or iterate on prompt set.

I attached the initial eval template (prompt_set_v1.txt) again. Laura — can you confirm you can run the two model variants and use chunk+kv-cache?

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: prompt_set_v1.txt
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Thompson <sam.thompson@acmehealth.com>, James Park <james.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Long-context evaluation next steps / model fit for Acme Health

Looping in some technical detail so the Acme team knows what to expect. Short notes: 

- Truncation & KV cache: For models that support KV cache across segments (redwood-extend family) we can keep a persistent KV state and stream subsequent chunks; this preserves cross-chunk context without full concatenation in memory. For llamax-65b (24k variant) we recommend semantic chunking at ~16k tokens with overlap=512 to cover boundary context; merge summaries with a 2-stage summarize->synthesize prompt.

- Fidelity checks: I’ll produce a CSV (long_context_eval_results.csv) with per-case ROUGE-1/2/L, BERTScore, and QA accuracy columns plus a free-text 'notes' column highlighting hallucinations. Example flagging rule: any QA answer whose normalized F1 < 0.6 is flagged for manual review.

- Quantization/Inference knobs: If cost is a concern we can run 4-bit quantized runs for a speed/cost baseline and full-precision runs for the fidelity sweep. Kernels: enable fused-attn kernel for the 128k model to avoid OOMs on long sequences.

Attachment: long_context_eval_tech_notes.pdf

I’ll start the two-variant run as soon as Sam shares the samples and confirms we can proceed with hosted telemetry.

—Laura
